milestones.title: The field gets its name
milestones.text: A summer workshop at Dartmouth, widely seen as the founding event of artificial intelligence as a field.

milestones.title: The first industrial robot goes to work
milestones.text: Unimate takes a job on a General Motors assembly line in Ewing Township, New Jersey.

milestones.title: A computer beats the world chess champion
milestones.text: IBM's Deep Blue defeats Garry Kasparov in a six-game rematch.

milestones.title: A machine wins at Jeopardy!
milestones.text: IBM's Watson beats champions Brad Rutter and Ken Jennings at the quiz show.

milestones.title: Deep learning takes off
milestones.text: AlexNet wins the ImageNet image-recognition contest with a top-5 error rate of 15.3%.

milestones.title: AlphaGo beats a Go champion
milestones.text: DeepMind's AlphaGo wins four of five games against Lee Sedol in Seoul.

milestones.title: The transformer
milestones.text: The paper "Attention Is All You Need" introduces the architecture behind today's large language models.
milestones.source_name: Wikipedia: Attention Is All You Need

milestones.title: AlphaFold 2 cracks protein folding
milestones.text: At the CASP14 competition, AlphaFold 2 predicts protein structures with far higher accuracy than any other entry.

milestones.title: A Nobel Prize for predicting protein structures
milestones.text: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry goes in part to Demis Hassabis and John Jumper for an AI model that solved a 50-year-old problem.

milestones.title: Five million industrial robots at work
milestones.text: The International Federation of Robotics reports a record 5 million industrial robots operating in the world's factories.
milestones.source_name: International Federation of Robotics (press release, Sep 24, 2026)
